# ALarms, Outcomes Telemetry with Timing (ALOTT)

## Description

ALOTT (ALarms, Outcomes Telemetry with Timing) is a pilot bedside-EMR database from two hospitals,
collected to support algorithms that predict emergency response team events. It pairs bedside
telemetry from 270 beds with electronic medical record data: admissions, diagnoses, ICU stays and bed
moves, labs, orders, medications and nursing flowsheets. MEDS-DEV uses the EMR tables only.[1]

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/alott/1.0.0/):

- **Access Policy**: Restricted access
- **License (for files)**: PhysioNet Restricted Health Data License Version 1.5.0
- **Data Use Agreement**: PhysioNet Restricted Health Data Use Agreement Version 1.5.0
- **Required training**: none

The ETL downloads the source files from PhysioNet. Set `DATASET_DOWNLOAD_USERNAME` and
`DATASET_DOWNLOAD_PASSWORD` to the credentials of an account with access before running it.

## Supported Tasks

The six blood `abnormal_lab` tasks, each extracted on the full 1.0.0 release:

- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/elevated_creatinine/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/hyponatremia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/metabolic_acidosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/anemia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/leukocytosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/thrombocytopenia/first_24h.yaml`

Two caveats apply to all six. Labs carry only a result *date* and are placed at 23:59:59, so the tasks'
24 h windows act as calendar days: the input window holds the labs of the admission day and the target
window those of the next day. The release has no birth date or age, so the tasks' adult filter excludes
no one.

Not supported:

- `mortality/in_icu/first_24h`: the release records no deaths, and no discharge destination marks one, so
    every label would be False. The ICU predicates are defined only because metabolic acidosis excludes
    stays with an ICU discharge in its first 48 h.
- `abnormal_lab/vital/hypotension/first_24h`: the EMR flowsheet has no blood pressure.

ALOTT has no demo, so the integration tests do not exercise these pairs.

## MEDS Transformation

[`ALOTT-MEDS`](https://github.com/rvandewater/ALOTT_MEDS) 0.0.1, pinned to its PyPI release in
`requirements.txt`, is a configuration-only [MEDS-Extract](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_extract) 0.7
pipeline, registered as `spec=ALOTT` for `meds-extract-run`. It transforms the EMR tables of the PhysioNet
release into MEDS; the telemetry is out of scope. There is no public demo, so only `build_full` is provided.
Version 0.0.1 includes [ALOTT_MEDS#2](https://github.com/rvandewater/ALOTT_MEDS/pull/2) (MEDS-Extract
0.7.1, aligned with the published 1.0.0 schema).[2] Notable properties of the conversion:

- **Dates are shifted** by a random offset of up to 180 days in either direction per patient; the time of
    day is kept.
- **Admissions** are `HOSPITAL_ADMISSION//<type>//<source>` and `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE//<destination>`. ICU
    stays are `ICU_ADMISSION` and `ICU_DISCHARGE`; the release does not say which unit.
- **No birth or death.** There is no `MEDS_BIRTH` or `MEDS_DEATH` event.
- **Labs** are `LAB//RESULT//<panel>//<component>`, timed at the end of the result date. The code carries
    no unit; the values are in US units (mg/dL, mmol/L, g/dL, K/uL). A chemistry panel reports each analyte
    under one of two component names, `BKR <ANALYTE>` or the plain name, and total CO2 as `CARBON DIOXIDE`
    or `CARBON DIOXIDE (CO2)`. The predicates list both names wherever a code occurs in at least 20
    subjects.

## Sources

1. [ALOTT v1.0.0 on PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/alott/1.0.0/)
2. [ALOTT-MEDS ETL](https://github.com/rvandewater/ALOTT_MEDS)

# AUMCdb

## Description

The first freely accessible intensive care database from within the European Union containing de-identified health data related to tens of thousands of European intensive care unit admissions, including demographics, vital signs, laboratory tests and medications.

## Access Requirements

Taken from [official website](https://amsterdammedicaldatascience.nl/amsterdamumcdb/#requesting-access):

- **Access Policy**: Fill out and sign the combined Access and End User License form.
- **License (for files)**: Specify the license under which the dataset files are distributed.
- **Data Use Agreement**: Agreement found [here](https://amsterdammedicaldatascience.nl/content/uploads/sites/2/2022/12/arfeula_v1.6.pdf).
- **Required training**: Valid training courses include the Data or Specimens Only Research (DSOR) course from CITI, the Basic Course for Clinical Investigators (BROK) from NFU or an equivalent course. The DSOR course may be taken free of charge and is also needed to gain access to the MIMIC and eICU intensive care databases from the USA.

## Supported Tasks

- `tasks/mortality/in_icu/first_24h.yaml`

## MEDS-transformation

[MEDS_transforms](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_transforms) now includes the AUMCdb example. Please refer to the [guide](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_transforms/tree/main/AUMC_Example).

## Sources

1. [AUMCdb dataset](https://amsterdammedicaldatascience.nl/amsterdamumcdb/)
2. [AUMCdb Research Paper](https://journals.lww.com/ccmjournal/fulltext/2021/06000/sharing_icu_patient_data_responsibly_under_the.16.aspx)
3. [AUMCdb Data Use Agreement](https://amsterdammedicaldatascience.nl/content/uploads/sites/2/2022/12/arfeula_v1.6.pdf)
4. [Data Repository](https://easy.dans.knaw.nl/ui/home)
5. [Code Repository](https://github.com/AmsterdamUMC/AmsterdamUMCdb)

## Disclaimer

Please refer to the data owners and the most up-to-date information when using this dataset in your research.

# COVID Data for Shared Learning (CDSL)

## Description

COVID Data for Shared Learning (CDSL) is a multimodal database of de-identified medical data from
4,479 patients hospitalized with confirmed or suspected COVID-19 in the Spanish HM Hospitales group
(2019-12-26 to 2021-02-13). It provides demographic, diagnostic, clinical and treatment tables, and
chest X-ray / CT images. MEDS-DEV uses the tabular data and the DICOM metadata, not the images.[1]

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/covid-data-shared-learning/1.0.0/):

- **Access Policy**: Contributor review
- **License (for files)**: PhysioNet Contributor Review Health Data License Version 1.5.0
- **Data Use Agreement**: PhysioNet Contributor Review Health Data Use Agreement Version 1.5.0
- **Required training**: CITI Data or Specimens Only Research

The ETL downloads the source files from PhysioNet. Set `DATASET_DOWNLOAD_USERNAME` and
`DATASET_DOWNLOAD_PASSWORD` to the credentials of an account with access before running it.

## Supported Tasks

Every current task except hypotension, each extracted on the full 1.0.0 release:

- `tasks/mortality/in_icu/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/elevated_creatinine/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/hyponatremia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/metabolic_acidosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/anemia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/leukocytosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/thrombocytopenia/first_24h.yaml`

`tasks/abnormal_lab/vital/hypotension/first_24h.yaml` is not supported: CDSL records systolic and diastolic
blood pressure but no mean arterial pressure. CDSL has no demo, so the integration tests do not exercise
these pairs.

## MEDS Transformation

[`CDSL-MEDS`](https://github.com/rvandewater/CDSL_MEDS) is a configuration-only
[MEDS-Extract](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_extract) 0.7 pipeline, registered as `spec=CDSL`.[2]
`requirements.txt` pins `CDSL-MEDS==0.0.1`, the newest code on PyPI: it was published from the `0.0.3` tag
after `0.0.2`, which is older code. Three CDSL files are Latin-1 encoded, so the build downloads first and
then runs `MEDS_extract-CDSL`, which stages a UTF-8 view of the download before extraction. There is no
public demo, so only `build_full` is provided. Notable properties of the conversion:

- **One hospital stay per subject.** `HOSPITAL_ADMISSION` and `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE//<destination>` are
    recorded to the day and placed at midnight, so "the first 24 hours" of the abnormal-lab tasks is the
    admission day. `ICU_ADMISSION` and `ICU_DISCHARGE` carry a time of day.
- **Death** is only a discharge destination. There is no `MEDS_DEATH`, so `predicates.yaml` overrides the
    tasks' `death` with `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE//Death`, timed at the (midnight) hospital discharge. For most
    ICU deaths that falls before the ICU discharge, so the in-ICU target window still sees it.
- **Age** is recorded in whole years at admission (`AGE_AT_ADMISSION`), and there is no `MEDS_BIRTH`. The
    abnormal-lab tasks exclude children by requiring no `birth` in the 18 years before admission, so
    `predicates.yaml` defines `birth` as an age below 18 at that admission. This excludes exactly the
    subjects younger than 18.
- **Labs** are `LAB//<item> -- <name>//<unit>` and are already in the tasks' units. Bicarbonate and total
    CO2 are reported only in blood-gas panels, so `bicarbonate` uses blood-gas HCO3.

## Sources

1. [CDSL v1.0.0 on PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/covid-data-shared-learning/1.0.0/)
    ([doi:10.13026/1176-6c44](https://doi.org/10.13026/1176-6c44))
2. [CDSL-MEDS ETL](https://github.com/rvandewater/CDSL_MEDS)
    ([doi:10.5281/zenodo.23676596](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23676596))

# EHRSHOT

## Description

A benchmark dataset of de-identified structured electronic health record data from Stanford Medicine containing longitudinal health records for 6,739 patients with 41.6 million coded clinical observations and 921,499 visits, designed for few-shot evaluation of foundation models on EHR data.[1][2]

## Access Requirements

Taken from [Stanford Shah Lab website](https://shahlab.stanford.edu/doku.php?id=ehrshot_license):

- **Access Policy**: Sign the EHRSHOT Credentialed Health Data License and Data Use Agreement[3][4]
- **License (for files)**: EHRSHOT Credentialed Health Data License Version 1.0 (modeled after Physionet Version 1.5.0)[3]
- **Data Use Agreement**: Agreement requires verified institutional affiliation and commitment to use data solely for lawful scientific research[5][3]
- **Required training**: Valid CITI training certification in human research subject protection and HIPAA regulations[4][3]
- **License Term**: 3 years from account creation date[3]
- **Code Sharing**: Agreement to contribute code associated with publications to open research repository[3]

## Supported Tasks

EHRSHOT includes 15 classification tasks organized into three categories as the benchmark dataset itself. However, here we use ACES-defined values to extract tasks from the dataset.

No MEDS-DEV task lists EHRShot in its `supported_datasets` yet. The current tasks exclude stays with a discharge
shortly after admission, which this release can't express (see below), so they can't be enabled for it as is.

## MEDS-transformation

EHRSHOT is available in three formats: Original (compatible with benchmark repository), MEDS (Medical Event Data Standard), and OMOP (full OMOP table dumps). The MEDS version contains the same exact data as the Original dataset but in MEDS-compatible format.[1]

### Which version `predicates.yaml` targets

The predicates target the **official MEDS release** (`EHRSHOT => MEDS ETL` 1.0, MEDS 0.3.3), with codes such as
`LOINC/2951-2`, `Visit/IP`, and `CARE_SITE/<id>`. They do not match a MEDS dataset converted from the OMOP
download with MEDS-Extract, which writes codes as `LOINC//2951-2` and conditions/visits with `//start` and
`//end` suffixes.

Notable properties of the official MEDS release:

- **No discharge events.** Visits are recorded only at their start (`Visit/IP`, `Visit/ER`, `Visit/ERIP`, ...),
    so `hospital_discharge` and `icu_discharge` are deliberately left undefined.
- **ICU stays can't be verified.** ICU care sites use the release's own care-site IDs, which differ from the
    OMOP `care_site` IDs, so the `icu_admission` IDs can't be checked against care-site names.
- **Birth and death** are `SNOMED/3950001` and `Condition Type/OMOP4822053` rather than `MEDS_BIRTH` and
    `MEDS_DEATH`; `predicates.yaml` overrides the tasks' `birth` and `death` predicates accordingly.
- **WBC:** `LOINC/6690-2` holds erythrocyte-scale values (MIL/uL); white-cell counts are under `LOINC/20584-9`.
- **Bicarbonate** uses total CO2 (`LOINC/2028-9`) and `LOINC/1959-6`; `LOINC/2021-4` is venous pCO2.

The OMOP-derived conversion has visit-end events, `MEDS_DEATH`, and care-site names, so it could support the
discharge- and ICU-based tasks, but it needs its own predicates and a reproducible build.

## Sources

1. [EHRSHOT Official Website](https://ehrshot.stanford.edu)
2. [EHRSHOT Research Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.02028v3)
3. [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/som-shahlab/ehrshot-benchmark)
4. [Redivis Dataset Portal](https://redivis.com/datasets/53gc-8rhx41kgt)
5. [Stanford AIMI Shared Datasets](https://stanfordaimi.azurewebsites.net/datasets/54c5d2a1-ef39-489e-b5f8-8f9e27e9750b)
6. [EHRSHOT License Agreement](https://shahlab.stanford.edu/doku.php?id=ehrshot_license)

## Disclaimer

Please refer to the data owners and the most up-to-date information when using this dataset in your research. The EHRSHOT dataset has not been reviewed or approved by the Food and Drug Administration and is for non-clinical, research and education use only.[3]

# HiRID: a high time-resolution ICU dataset

## Description

HiRID holds 33,905 admissions to the Department of Intensive Care Medicine of the Bern University Hospital,
Switzerland, an interdisciplinary 60-bed unit, between January 2008 and June 2016. It contains de-identified
demographics and 681 routinely collected physiological variables, diagnostic test results and treatment
parameters, with bedside measurements recorded as often as every two minutes. It was developed by the Swiss
Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) Zürich and the ICU.[1][2] MEDS-DEV uses release 1.1.1.

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/hirid/1.1.1/):

- **Access Policy**: Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files, and each study must be
    reviewed by the HiRID contributors
- **License (for files)**: PhysioNet Contributor Review Health Data License 1.5.0
- **Data Use Agreement**: PhysioNet Contributor Review Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0
- **Required training**: CITI Data or Specimens Only Research

The ETL downloads the three release files it reads (about 7 GB) from PhysioNet. Set
`DATASET_DOWNLOAD_USERNAME` and `DATASET_DOWNLOAD_PASSWORD` to the credentials of an account with access
before running it. To reuse an existing download, pass its directory as `raw_input_dir`: files whose checksum
matches PhysioNet's manifest are not downloaded again, although the credentials are still needed to fetch the
manifest.

## Supported Tasks

Every current task, each extracted on the full 1.1.1 release:

- `tasks/mortality/in_icu/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/elevated_creatinine/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/hyponatremia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/metabolic_acidosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/anemia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/leukocytosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/thrombocytopenia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/vital/hypotension/first_24h.yaml`

The hospital-level tasks use the ICU stay (see below), so they predict from the first 24 hours of the ICU stay
and require a stay of at least 48 hours.

HiRID has no demo, so the integration tests do not exercise these pairs.

## MEDS Transformation

[`HIRID-MEDS`](https://github.com/rvandewater/HIRID_MEDS) is a pure-config
[MEDS-Extract](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_extract) pipeline, registered as `spec=HIRID` for
`meds-extract-run`.[3] HiRID has no public demo, so only `build_full` is provided. The build sets
`POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY=streaming`, which keeps it under 10 GB of memory; without it, subject sharding runs out
of memory on a 24 GB machine. Extracts made with HIRID-MEDS 0.0.1–0.0.4 duplicate, mislabel and drop some observation events, so they
should be rebuilt. Notable properties of the conversion:

- **ICU stays only.** Each subject is one ICU admission. `HOSPITAL_ADMISSION` is the ICU admission time and
    `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE` is the time of the subject's last observation, since HiRID records no discharge time.
    The ETL keeps these names from its earlier releases. HiRID records no hospital admission or discharge, so
    the hospital-level tasks use the ICU stay, as they do for SICdb.
- **Dates are shifted** into the future, keeping the order and spacing of events within a subject.
- **Birth and death** are `MEDS_BIRTH` and `MEDS_DEATH`, so the tasks' default predicates apply. The birth is
    estimated from the age at admission, which HiRID records in 5-year bins from 20 to 90, so it can be off by
    up to about 5 years. `MEDS_DEATH` is placed at the last observation when the discharge status is `dead`,
    which makes it a death in the ICU. It coincides with `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE`.
- **Observations** are `OBSERVATION//<variable name>//<unit>`, using HiRID's variable reference. Lab values
    are in SI units, so two thresholds are converted: creatinine to 114.92 µmol/L (1.3 mg/dL) and hemoglobin to
    130 g/L (13 g/dL). HiRID has no serum bicarbonate, so `bicarbonate` uses arterial blood-gas bicarbonate. The
    LOINC codes of the lab variables come from the suMEDS rules file that HIRID-MEDS ships.
- **Mean arterial pressure** combines the invasive and non-invasive readings. The invasive signal is recorded
    as often as every two minutes, so `abnormally_low_map` flags a single reading below 65 mmHg. Few stays have
    no such reading in their first 24 hours, so the hypotension cohort is small.

## Sources

1. [HiRID 1.1.1 on PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/hirid/1.1.1/)
    ([doi:10.13026/nkwc-js72](https://doi.org/10.13026/nkwc-js72))
2. Hyland et al.,
    [Early prediction of circulatory failure in the intensive care unit using machine learning](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-020-0789-4),
    Nature Medicine 26, 364–373 (2020)
3. [HIRID-MEDS ETL](https://github.com/rvandewater/HIRID_MEDS)

# INSPECT: Integrating Numerous Sources for Prognostic Evaluation of Clinical Timelines

## Description

INSPECT is a multimodal dataset from Stanford Medicine of 19,402 patients with 23,248 CT pulmonary
angiography (CTPA) studies performed to diagnose pulmonary embolism. It pairs the CT images and radiology
report impressions with each patient's longitudinal structured EHR data, released as STARR-OMOP tables
(Stanford's research data repository in the OMOP Common Data Model).[1][2] MEDS-DEV uses only the
structured EHR modality.

## Access Requirements

Taken from the [INSPECT website](https://som-shahlab.github.io/inspect-website/) and
[Stanford AIMI](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/inspect-Multimodal-Dataset-for-Pulmonary-Embolism-Diagnosis-and-Prognosis):

- **Access Policy**: The de-identified dataset is available under a data use agreement.[1][3]
- **Permitted use**: Non-commercial research use only.[1][3]
- **Distribution**: The EHR tables are distributed through Stanford's Redivis platform; the CT images
    through the Stanford AIMI shared datasets portal.[1][3]
- **Dataset DOI**: [10.71718/aqrb-et67](https://doi.org/10.71718/aqrb-et67).[3]

## Supported Tasks

No MEDS-DEV task lists INSPECT in its `supported_datasets` yet. Every current task excludes stays with a
hospital or ICU discharge shortly after admission, and this conversion has no discharge events (see below), so
`predicates.yaml` leaves `hospital_discharge` and `icu_discharge` undefined rather than approximating them.

## MEDS Transformation

The INSPECT EHR data is distributed in OMOP form. The predicates target a conversion of the INSPECT STARR-OMOP
release with [`meds_etl`](https://github.com/Medical-Event-Data-Standard/meds_etl)'s `meds_etl_omop` (version
`0.3.9.dev11+gba0eec1`, MEDS 0.3.3), which prefers source concepts over standard ones and writes codes as
`<vocabulary_id>/<concept_code>`, e.g. `LOINC/2951-2`. They do not match a conversion with MEDS-Extract, which
writes codes such as `LOINC//2951-2` and adds `//start` and `//end` events. `build_full` is not automated
because the conversion has not been verified against a published `meds_etl` release, so convert the download
yourself and pass the MEDS directory as `dataset_dir`. The conversion does not write
`metadata/subject_splits.parquet`, so add one before training models.

The predicates were chosen from a privacy-preserving code summary made with
[suMEDS](https://github.com/rvandewater/suMEDS) (codes seen in at least 20 subjects, with per-code and per-unit
value statistics), without inspecting patient-level data. Notable properties of the conversion:

- **Hospital admissions** are the `visit_occurrence` events, coded with Stanford source visit concepts
    `STANFORD_VISIT/<patient class>|<admission type>|<encounter type>`. `hospital_admission` matches hospital
    encounters with an inpatient patient class (`Inpatient`, `Private (Gen/Acute) (I)`, `Ward (Gen/Acute) (I)`,
    `Intensive Care (IC)`, `Surgery Admit`) for any admission type. Observation, pre-admission, skilled-nursing,
    and historical (legacy-system) encounters are excluded, as are appointments, anesthesia records, and lab
    draws recorded under an inpatient class.
- **ICU admissions** are `visit_detail` unit segments with the standard concept `Visit/OMOP4822460` (OMOP
    concept 32037, "Intensive Care"). Several segments can belong to one ICU stay. `CMS Place of Service/OMOP4822038`
    ("Inpatient Cardiac Care Facility") is not counted as ICU care.
- **No discharge events.** `meds_etl.omop` keeps visit end times only in the `end` column of the visit's start
    event, which ACES can't use, and writes a separate end-of-visit event only from `discharged_to_concept_id`,
    for which the conversion has no events.
- **Birth and death** are `MEDS_BIRTH` and `MEDS_DEATH`, so the tasks' default predicates apply.
- **Labs and vitals** use LOINC codes measured directly in blood, serum, or plasma, with units equivalent to
    the task thresholds: creatinine `LOINC/2160-0`; sodium `LOINC/2951-2`, `LOINC/2947-0`; bicarbonate as total
    CO2 `LOINC/2028-9`; hemoglobin `LOINC/718-7`, `LOINC/30313-1`; WBC `LOINC/20584-9`; platelets `LOINC/777-3`;
    and mean blood pressure `LOINC/8478-0`. `LOINC/6690-2` (leukocytes) is excluded because part of its values
    are reported per uL rather than 10^3/uL.

A conversion that emits visit-end events would support the discharge-based tasks, but it needs its own
predicates.

## Sources

1. [INSPECT website](https://som-shahlab.github.io/inspect-website/)
2. [INSPECT paper (arXiv:2311.10798)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10798), NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks
    Track
3. [INSPECT on Stanford AIMI](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/inspect-Multimodal-Dataset-for-Pulmonary-Embolism-Diagnosis-and-Prognosis)
4. [INSPECT benchmark code](https://github.com/som-shahlab/INSPECT_public)

# INSPIRE: a publicly available research dataset for perioperative medicine

## Description

The INSPIRE dataset is a publicly available research dataset in perioperative medicine, which includes approximately 130,000 cases (50% of all surgical cases) who underwent anesthesia for surgery at an academic institution in South Korea between 2011 and 2020. This comprehensive dataset includes patient characteristics such as age, sex, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status classification, diagnosis, surgical procedure code, department, and type of anesthesia. It also includes vital signs in the operating theatre, general wards, and intensive care units (ICUs), laboratory results from six months before admission to six months after discharge, and medication during hospitalization. Complications include total hospital and ICU length of stay and in-hospital death.[1]

## Access Requirements

- **Data Use Agreement**: Korea Credentialed Health Data Agreement 1.0.0; the data may be used for research purposes only.[1,2]

# Multimodal Clinical Monitoring in the Emergency Department (MC-MED)

## Description

MC-MED holds 118,385 adult emergency department (ED) visits by 70,545 patients at Stanford Health Care
between 2020 and 2022. For each visit it contains demographics, triage, the ED course and dispositions, the
primary ED diagnoses, orders and medication administrations, laboratory results, radiology report
impressions, charted and monitor vital signs, past medical history, and home medications, together with
continuous ECG, photoplethysmography and respiration waveforms.[1][2] MEDS-DEV uses release 1.0.1.

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/mc-med/1.0.1/):

- **Access Policy**: Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files
- **License (for files)**: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0
- **Data Use Agreement**: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0
- **Required training**: CITI Data or Specimens Only Research

The ETL downloads the tabular files of the release from PhysioNet (not the waveforms). Set
`DATASET_DOWNLOAD_USERNAME` and `DATASET_DOWNLOAD_PASSWORD` to the credentials of an account with access
before running it.

## Supported Tasks

None of the current tasks. Every one of them needs a hospital or ICU stay, and MC-MED records the ED visit
only:

- `tasks/mortality/in_icu/first_24h.yaml` and
    `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/metabolic_acidosis/first_24h.yaml` follow an ICU stay. MC-MED
    identifies the 2,766 visits (2.3%) admitted from the ED to the ICU, so `icu_admission` is
    `ED_DISPOSITION//ICU`, the disposition decision. But it records no ICU discharge time and no labs or vital
    signs after ED departure, so `icu_discharge` is undefined and the tasks cannot be extracted.
- The other abnormal-lab tasks and `tasks/abnormal_lab/vital/hypotension/first_24h.yaml` start at the hospital
    admission and label a measurement 24 to 48 hours later. MC-MED's labs and vital signs end at ED
    departure, so only patients still boarding in the ED more than a day after their admission order
    qualify. On the full release each of these tasks extracts fewer than 100 samples from about 48,000
    admissions, too few and too unusual a group to evaluate on.

The predicates the tasks use are defined anyway, so ED-specific tasks can be added later.

## MEDS Transformation

[`MC-MED-MEDS`](https://github.com/rvandewater/MC_MED_MEDS) is a pure-config
[MEDS-Extract](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_extract) pipeline, registered as `spec=MC-MED`. It is
run with [suMEDS](https://github.com/rvandewater/SumMEDS)' `suMEDS-extract`, which runs `meds-extract-run`
and then adds the official ICD-10-CM and ICD-9-CM titles and parents to `metadata/codes.parquet`. MC-MED has
no public demo, so only `build_full` is provided.[3] Notable properties of the conversion:

- **Dates are shifted** per patient into 2150–2350 by the dataset authors, keeping the season, so only
    time differences within one subject carry meaning.
- **One visit is one ED encounter**, from `ED_ARRIVAL//<means of arrival>` to `ED_DEPARTURE`, and every
    visit-scoped event carries the visit's `CSN` in a `csn` column. Triage has no time of its own and is placed
    at arrival.
- **Hospital and ICU admission, and discharge.** `HOSPITAL_ADMISSION//<service>` is the admission order of
    a visit admitted from the ED, and `ED_DISPOSITION//ICU` marks the decision to admit it to the ICU, a median
    of 2.3 h before the patient leaves the ED. MC-MED has no discharge time, so `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE//<disposition>` is
    reconstructed from the whole-day hospital length of stay, never earlier than ED departure. It is
    accurate to about a day.
- **Birth and death.** There is no `MEDS_BIRTH`: MC-MED gives only an age perturbed by up to 2 years at each
    visit, as an `AGE` event. `MEDS_DEATH` marks in-hospital deaths only (a discharge disposition of
    `Expired`), at the reconstructed discharge time, so a subject without one is not known to be alive.
- **Labs** are `LAB//<component name>//<unit>`, from the ED visit only, with the parsed value as
    `numeric_value` and the raw result as `text_value`. Vital signs are `VITAL//<measure>//{Chart,Monitor}`;
    monitor values are means over the preceding minute.
- **Diagnoses** are dotted ICD codes: `ED_DIAGNOSIS//ICD10CM//<code>` and `ED_DIAGNOSIS//ICD9CM//<code>`
    for the visit, and `PMH//ICD10CM//<code>` and `PMH//ICD9CM//<code>` for past medical history.

## Sources

1. [MC-MED 1.0.1 on PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/mc-med/1.0.1/)
    ([doi:10.13026/wvyw-g663](https://doi.org/10.13026/wvyw-g663))
2. Kansal et al.,
    [MC-MED, multimodal clinical monitoring in the emergency department](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-05419-5),
    Scientific Data 12 (2025)
3. [MC-MED-MEDS ETL](https://github.com/rvandewater/MC_MED_MEDS)

data.readme:
# MIMIC-IV: Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV

## Description

MIMIC-IV is a large deidentified dataset of patients admitted to the emergency department or an intensive
care unit at the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, MA, between 2008 and 2022. It contains
data for over 65,000 patients admitted to an ICU and over 200,000 patients admitted to the emergency
department.[1][2] Its `hosp` module comes from the hospital-wide EHR and its `icu` module from the
MetaVision ICU clinical information system. As of v3.0, PhysioNet counts 364,627 unique individuals with
546,028 hospitalizations and 94,458 ICU stays. MEDS-DEV uses release 3.1 (October 2024), which fixes lab
`itemid`s that changed unintentionally in 3.0 and removes two `subject_id`s missing from `patients`.

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/mimiciv/3.1/):

- **Access Policy**: Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files
- **License (for files)**: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0
- **Data Use Agreement**: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0
- **Required training**: CITI Data or Specimens Only Research

The ETL downloads the release from PhysioNet. Set `DATASET_DOWNLOAD_USERNAME` and
`DATASET_DOWNLOAD_PASSWORD` to the credentials of an account with access before running it, or pass an
existing download as `raw_input_dir`.

The [MIMIC-IV demo](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-demo/2.2/) (version 2.2, 100 patients) is open
access under the Open Data Commons Open Database License 1.0, so the demo build needs no credentials.[3]

## Supported Tasks

Every current task:

- `tasks/mortality/in_icu/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/elevated_creatinine/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/hyponatremia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/metabolic_acidosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/anemia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/leukocytosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/thrombocytopenia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/vital/hypotension/first_24h.yaml`

The integration tests and CI run every task and model on the demo build.

## MEDS Transformation

[`MIMIC-IV-MEDS`](https://github.com/Medical-Event-Data-Standard/MIMIC_IV_MEDS) 0.1.0 provides the
`MEDS_extract-MIMIC_IV` command, which downloads the release, runs a pre-MEDS step over the raw tables and
then builds the MEDS dataset with MEDS-Transforms.[4] `build_demo` passes `do_demo=True`, which builds the
open demo instead of the full release. Notable properties of the conversion:

- **Visits.** `HOSPITAL_ADMISSION//<admission type>//<admission location>` and
    `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE//<discharge location>` mark hospital stays, `ICU_ADMISSION//<first care unit>` and
    `ICU_DISCHARGE//<last care unit>` mark ICU stays, and `ED_REGISTRATION` and `ED_OUT` mark the emergency
    department visit before an admission. The admission and discharge predicates match these by prefix.
- **Measurements** keep MIMIC-IV's `itemid` and unit. Hospital lab results (`hosp/labevents`) are
    `LAB//RESULT//<itemid>//<unit>`, and values charted in the ICU (`icu/chartevents`), including vital
    signs, are `LAB//<itemid>//<unit>`. Each lab predicate therefore combines the hospital lab with the
    matching ICU chart item, and matches only the unit listed. The abnormal thresholds are in the units of
    the tasks, so none is converted.
- **Birth and death** are `MEDS_BIRTH` and `MEDS_DEATH`, so the tasks' default predicates apply. The birth
    year is `anchor_year - anchor_age`, so births have year precision, and patients over 89 have an
    `anchor_age` of 91. A death is placed at the earliest in-hospital `deathtime`, or else at the date of
    death in `patients`, which also covers deaths up to one year after hospital or ED discharge from state
    records.
- **Dates are shifted** into 2100–2200 by one random offset per patient, which keeps the order and spacing
    of each patient's events.

| Predicate     | Hospital lab (`LAB//RESULT//…`)     | ICU chart (`LAB//…`)                                                 | Abnormal    |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `creatinine`  | 50912, 52546 (creatinine, mg/dL)    | none                                                                 | > 1.3 mg/dL |

# Paediatric Intensive Care (PIC) Database

## Description

The Paediatric Intensive Care (PIC) database is a de-identified, paediatric-specific critical-care
database of 12,881 neonatal and paediatric patients and 13,449 hospital admissions at the Children's
Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine (2010–2018). It follows the MIMIC structure:
admissions, ICU stays, laboratory and chart events, inputs and outputs, prescriptions, microbiology,
diagnoses and surgery records.[1][2]

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/picdb/1.1.0/):

- **Access Policy**: Credentialed access
- **License (for files)**: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License Version 1.5.0
- **Data Use Agreement**: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement Version 1.5.0
- **Required training**: CITI Data or Specimens Only Research

The ETL downloads the source files from PhysioNet. Set `DATASET_DOWNLOAD_USERNAME` and
`DATASET_DOWNLOAD_PASSWORD` to the credentials of an account with access before running it.

## Supported Tasks

Extracted on the full 1.1.0 release:

- `tasks/mortality/in_icu/first_24h.yaml`: ICU stays carry their unit (`ICU_ADMISSION//<unit>` for CICU,
    General ICU, NICU, PICU and SICU), and `MEDS_DEATH` coincides with the last ICU discharge for 968 of the
    971 deaths. Almost a quarter of the ICU stays start in the NICU; a variant without them may be worth a
    separate task.

The `abnormal_lab` tasks are not supported, although they extract without errors. They exclude patients aged
18 or younger and use adult thresholds, and PIC has no admission at 18 or older. Their only rows come from 68
admissions of newborns recorded up to a day before the recorded time of birth, which the age window does not
catch. The lab codes for a paediatric variant are creatinine `LAB//5041//μmol/L` and `LAB//5032//μmol/L`
(LOINC 2160-0), sodium `LAB//5230//mmol/L` (whole blood, LOINC 2947-0), bicarbonate `LAB//5248//mmol/L` and
`LAB//5224//mmol/L` (blood gas), hemoglobin `LAB//5099//g/L` (LOINC 718-7) and `LAB//5257//g/L` (blood gas),
WBC `LAB//5141//×10^9/L` (LOINC 26464-8) and platelets `LAB//5129//×10^9/L` (LOINC 777-3). There is no ICU
mean arterial pressure: the chart data has only systolic and diastolic pressure, and MAP is recorded only
during surgery (`SURGERY_VITAL//SV5`, `SURGERY_VITAL//SV12`).

PICdb has no demo, so the integration tests do not exercise these pairs.

## MEDS Transformation

[`PICdb-MEDS`](https://github.com/rvandewater/PICdb_MEDS) is a pure-config
[MEDS-Extract](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_extract) 0.7 pipeline, registered as `spec=PICdb` for
`meds-extract-run`. There is no public demo, so only `build_full` is provided.[3] MEDS-DEV uses PICdb-MEDS
0.0.3, the first release whose wheel ships `event_configs.yaml` (0.0.1 lacks it, so its `spec=PICdb` entry
point cannot load). It also describes every code in `metadata/codes.parquet`. Notable properties of the
conversion:

- **Dates are shifted** 50–100 years into the future per patient, so only time differences within one
    subject carry meaning.
- **Admissions and stays.** `HOSPITAL_ADMISSION//<department>` and `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE//<department>` bound
    each hospital admission, and `ICU_ADMISSION//<unit>` and `ICU_DISCHARGE//<unit>` each ICU stay.
- **Birth and death** are `MEDS_BIRTH` and `MEDS_DEATH`, so the tasks' default predicates apply.
- **Labs** are `LAB//<ITEMID>//<unit>`, named in `metadata/codes.parquet` with the `LOINC/` parents of
    `D_LABITEMS`. Chart events are `CHART//<ITEMID>//<unit>`.

## Sources

1. [PIC database v1.1.0 on PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/picdb/1.1.0/)
2. [Zeng et al., PIC, a paediatric-specific intensive care database, Scientific Data 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0355-4)
3. [PICdb-MEDS ETL](https://github.com/rvandewater/PICdb_MEDS)

# Salzburg Intensive Care database (SICdb)

## Description

The Salzburg Intensive Care database (SICdb) holds more than 27,000 intensive care admissions from four
ICUs at the University Hospital Salzburg, collected between 2013 and 2021. It covers general and surgical
intensive care, including data on the surgery preceding an admission, and contains case information,
diagnoses, laboratory results, medications, devices, and vital signs as both hourly aggregates and
minute-resolution signals.[1][2] MEDS-DEV uses release 1.0.8.

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/sicdb/1.0.8/):

- **Access Policy**: Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files, and each study must be
    reviewed by the SICdb contributors
- **License (for files)**: PhysioNet Contributor Review Health Data License 1.5.0
- **Data Use Agreement**: PhysioNet Contributor Review Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0
- **Required training**: CITI Data or Specimens Only Research

The ETL downloads the release from PhysioNet. Set `DATASET_DOWNLOAD_USERNAME` and
`DATASET_DOWNLOAD_PASSWORD` to the credentials of an account with access before running it. To reuse an
existing download, pass its directory (the one holding `SHA256SUMS.txt`) as `raw_input_dir`: files whose
checksum matches PhysioNet's manifest are not downloaded again, although the credentials are still needed
to fetch the manifest.

## Supported Tasks

Every current task, each extracted on the full 1.0.8 release:

- `tasks/mortality/in_icu/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/elevated_creatinine/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/hyponatremia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/metabolic_acidosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/anemia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/leukocytosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/thrombocytopenia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/vital/hypotension/first_24h.yaml`

SICdb has no demo, so the integration tests do not exercise these pairs.

## MEDS Transformation

[`SICdb-MEDS`](https://github.com/rvandewater/SICdb_MEDS) is a pure-config
[MEDS-Extract](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_extract) pipeline, registered as `spec=SICdb` for
`meds-extract-run`. SICdb has no public demo, so only `build_full` is provided.[3] Notable properties of the
conversion:

- **Dates are not real.** SICdb gives offsets in seconds, not dates. Every patient's first admission is
    placed on 2017-07-02 and everything else keeps its offset from it, so only time differences within one
    subject carry meaning. The real admission year is kept as an `ADMISSION_YEAR//<year>` event.
- **One case is one ICU admission** with its preceding surgery, if any. `ADMISSION//<urgency>` opens the
    case and is used as the hospital admission, since SICdb records no hospital admission time. `ICU_ADMISSION` marks the first transfer to an intensive or intermediate care
    ward, and `DISCHARGE//<state>` closes the case on leaving the ICU. `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE//<type>` is
    recorded to the day and placed at noon.
- **Birth and death** are `MEDS_BIRTH` and `MEDS_DEATH`, so the tasks' default predicates apply. The birth
    is estimated from the age at the first admission, which SICdb records in whole years and caps at 90.
    SICdb records a death only when it happens within a year of the admission.
- **Labs** are `LAB//<LaboratoryID>//<specimen>`, with the specimen `ARTERIAL` for blood-gas analyses and
    `UNSPEC` otherwise. Their names, units, and LOINC parent codes are in `metadata/codes.parquet`. SICdb has
    no serum bicarbonate, so `bicarbonate` uses blood-gas bicarbonate.
- **Vital signs** are `VITAL//<DataID>` and are hourly aggregates, so `abnormally_low_map` flags an hour
    whose mean pressure is below 65 mmHg rather than a single reading.

## Sources

1. [SICdb 1.0.8 on PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/sicdb/1.0.8/)
    ([doi:10.13026/8m72-6j83](https://doi.org/10.13026/8m72-6j83))
2. Rodemund et al.,
    [Harnessing Big Data in Critical Care: Exploring a New European Dataset](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-024-03164-9),
    Scientific Data 11, 320 (2024)
3. [SICdb-MEDS ETL](https://github.com/rvandewater/SICdb_MEDS)

# Zigong Fourth People's Hospital ICU Infection Database

## Description

The Zigong database is a de-identified critical-care database of 2,790 ICU patients with infection,
one hospital admission each, from Zigong Fourth People's Hospital in Sichuan, China. It covers
baseline characteristics, transfers, laboratory results, prescriptions, nursing charts, diagnoses,
and outcomes including follow-up vital status.[1][2] MEDS-DEV uses release 1.1.

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/icu-infection-zigong-fourth/1.1/):

- **Access Policy**: Credentialed access
- **License (for files)**: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License Version 1.5.0
- **Data Use Agreement**: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement Version 1.5.0
- **Required training**: CITI Data or Specimens Only Research

The ETL downloads the source files from PhysioNet. Set `DATASET_DOWNLOAD_USERNAME` and
`DATASET_DOWNLOAD_PASSWORD` to the credentials of an account with access before running it.

## Supported Tasks

Seven of the eight current tasks, each extracted on the full 1.1 release:

- `tasks/mortality/in_icu/first_24h.yaml`, for subjects admitted straight into an ICU department only
    (see below).
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/elevated_creatinine/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/hyponatremia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/blood_chemistry/metabolic_acidosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/anemia/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/leukocytosis/first_24h.yaml`
- `tasks/abnormal_lab/cbc/thrombocytopenia/first_24h.yaml`

`tasks/abnormal_lab/vital/hypotension/first_24h.yaml` is not supported: the raw MAP column holds only
unit strings, and ACES cannot derive MAP from systolic and diastolic pressure.

Zigong has no demo, so the integration tests do not exercise these pairs.

## MEDS Transformation

[`Zigong-MEDS`](https://github.com/rvandewater/ZIGONG_MEDS) 0.3.0 is a pure-config
[MEDS-Extract](https://github.com/mmcdermott/MEDS_extract) 0.7 pipeline, registered as `spec=Zigong` for
`meds-extract-run`. Zigong has no public demo, so only `build_full` is provided.[3] Notable properties of
the conversion:

- **Dates are not real.** Every source time is an offset in hours from hospital admission, placed on a
    shared anchor (1970-01-01 00:00 = admission). Each subject has exactly one admission.
- **One admission per subject.** `HOSPITAL_ADMISSION` and `HOSPITAL_DISCHARGE` bound the stay, and
    `ICU_DISCHARGE` marks the end of the ICU stay. The release records no ICU admission time, and its
    transfer table repeats rows within a stay
    ([ZIGONG_MEDS#3](https://github.com/rvandewater/ZIGONG_MEDS/issues/3)). `icu_admission` is therefore the
    admission of subjects whose admission department is an ICU (EICU, ICU, RICU, SICU or one of the two NICUs),
    about half of the cohort, at hospital admission. Subjects transferred into an ICU later are not in the
    in-ICU mortality cohort.
- **Death** is `MEDS_DEATH`, so the tasks' default `death` predicate applies. `Death_Date` has day precision
    and includes deaths at follow-up after discharge. The in-ICU mortality target ends at ICU discharge, so
    follow-up deaths do not count, but a death dated on the day of ICU discharge counts as an ICU death.
- **Age, not birth.** There is no `MEDS_BIRTH`, only `AGE_AT_ADMISSION` in years. `birth` matches that event
    for subjects younger than 18, so the abnormal-lab tasks' exclusion of children still applies.
- **Labs** are `LAB//<panel>//<item>//<unit>` in SI units, so the creatinine (umol/L) and hemoglobin (g/L)
    thresholds are converted from the tasks' US units. Sodium is the serum electrolyte panel. Bicarbonate is
    serum total CO2 plus measured blood-gas bicarbonate. Blood-gas hemoglobin is left out, because two of its
    codes are labelled g/L but hold g/dL values.

## Sources

1. [Zigong ICU infection database v1.1 on PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/icu-infection-zigong-fourth/1.1/)
2. [Xu et al., Critical Care Database Comprising Patients With Infection, Frontiers in Public Health 2022](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2022.852410)
3. [Zigong-MEDS ETL](https://github.com/rvandewater/ZIGONG_MEDS)

# eICU Collaborative Research Database

## Description

The eICU Collaborative Research Database is a multi-center database comprising de-identified health data associated with over 200,000 admissions to ICUs across the United States between 2014-2015. The database includes vital sign measurements, care plan documentation, severity of illness measures, diagnosis information, and treatment information. Data is collected through the Philips eICU program, a critical care telehealth program that delivers information to caregivers at the bedside.[1]

## Access Requirements

Taken from [PhysioNet](https://physionet.org/content/eicu-crd/2.0/):
